Language.Name: TypeScript
Language.Usage: Primary implementation language for the workflow runtime, validators, and CLI surface.

Language.Name: JSON / JSONL
Language.Usage: Persist workflow state, transition events, policies, and sidecar trace artifacts.

Language.Name: GRACE XML-like markup
Language.Usage: Retained as the durable artifact layer for handoffs, CWOs, approvals, and execution evidence.

Framework.Name: Node.js
Framework.Usage: Runtime for the workflow engine, validators, and local CLI orchestration.

Framework.Name: LangGraph
Framework.Usage: State-machine orchestration engine with durable checkpoints, interrupts, and explicit node routing.

Framework.Name: node:test
Framework.Usage: Framework and workflow contract tests without external test runner dependencies.

Decision.Title: State-machine-first orchestration
Decision.Description: GRACE uses an explicit workflow state machine as the source of control for process movement.
Decision.Rationale: Prompt-only skill loading is not strong enough to guarantee mandatory governance behavior.

Decision.Title: LangGraph as workflow runtime
Decision.Description: LangGraph is used as the orchestration runtime for typed state, guarded transitions, interrupts, and resumable execution.
Decision.Rationale: It gives durable workflow control while still accommodating bounded agent execution nodes.

Decision.Title: Policy-as-code guard layer
Decision.Description: Actor permissions, transition rules, and guard requirements are stored as machine-readable policies evaluated before transition execution.
Decision.Rationale: Governance must be executable and versioned separately from agent prompts.

Decision.Title: Existing GRACE artifacts remain the evidence layer
Decision.Description: Handoffs, approvals, CWOs, execution traces, skill traces, verification reports, and W11 artifacts remain durable evidence and transition effects.
Decision.Rationale: GRACE should strengthen process control without throwing away the current artifact model.

Decision.Title: Product isolation during v2 incubation
Decision.Description: `grace` evolves in its own workspace and does not mutate active demo products except via explicit integration slices.
Decision.Rationale: The new control architecture should be developed and validated in isolation before framework-wide adoption.

Decision.Title: Semantic-slice-first delivery
Decision.Description: Implementation is split by one `FC-*` per coder chunk, or at most one to two `BA-*` inside the same `FC-*`.
Decision.Rationale: The v2 engine itself must obey the same strict chunking and traceability discipline it intends to enforce.

Decision.Title: Reuse v1 validators through bounded adapters
Decision.Description: Existing v1 validators and trace tools are invoked through explicit v2 adapter surfaces while migration is in progress.
Decision.Rationale: This preserves proven validation behavior without allowing legacy scripts to remain the source of process control.

Decision.Title: Legacy onboarding uses overlay workspaces
Decision.Description: External legacy repositories are governed through overlay workspaces that materialize GRACE state, policy, reports, and traceability artifacts without forcing immediate source-tree mutation.
Decision.Rationale: An overlay-first model lets GRACE control process and semantics for legacy codebases before any risky invasive rewrite begins.
